To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pattern formation of positive dc corona driven by half-wave rectified voltages is similar to dc corona driven with pure dc voltage, but the pattern formation is more complex.
the PRPD patterns of positive corona driven by DC voltages containing a half-wave rectified ripple are characterized by five patterns.

the different stages of PRPDPs for positive point to point corona driven by DC voltages containing a half-wave rectified ripple can be identified and that the appearance of patterns can be explained with support of measured discharge pulses and underlying physical processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the PRPD patterns for corona driven by positive dc voltages containing ripples.
the analysis of the pattern formation of a positive corona driven by dc voltage containing ripple.
the development of pattern formation of the partial discharge patterns in a positive point to plane configuration, which is driven by a half-wave rectified dc voltage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pattern formation is mainly governed by the discharge current and the voltage amplitude.

the pattern formation is caused by the superposition of the different discharge sources, namely the positive corona, the positive and the negative streamers, which appear during positive and negative polarity voltage application, and the negative corona, which is present only during negative voltage polarity.
the patterns can be used as a tool for the identification of the four stages of corona onset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patterns are a result of a superposition of discharge pulses.
the pattern formation is not only dependent on the voltage waveform but also on the discharge current.

the pattern recognition of PRPDs from positive corona driven by dc voltage containing a half wave rectification is possible and the patterns can be explained with the physical processes of the corona.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pattern formation is a complex process, which is influenced by the discharge current, the applied voltage, the geometry of the discharge gap, and the gas mixture.
the PRPD patterns are strongly influenced by the applied voltage.
a dc voltage containing a superimposed ripple is a suitable test voltage to investigate the different stages of corona development and to study the appearance of different discharge patterns.
